Syracuse men’s soccer knocks off Sacred Heart in NCAA Tournament thriller

Men’s soccer picks up NCAA Tournament win over Sacred Heart

Orange advance to face No. 1 Georgetown after 3-2 victory

Story by Chadi Tolaimate / Photos by Isaac Williams
Published: November 19, 2026
Photo by Isaac Williams
Syracuse players celebrated with fans after their 3-2 victory over Sacred Heart in the first round of the NCAA Division I Men’s Soccer Championship at SU Soccer Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. Syracuse advanced to face No. 1 seed Georgetown in the second round on Sunday, Nov. 22. (Isaac Williams/The NewsHouse)

Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:24
Instaread

A day shy of the one-year anniversary of its home loss to Hofstra in the opening round of the 2025 NCAA Tournament, Syracuse men’s soccer mended broken hearts with a 3-2 down-to-the-wire victory over The Pioneers.

For the nine Syracuse players who returned from last season, tonight’s victory, and the ensuing skol-style celebration with Otto’s Army, carried extra meaning. 

“The guys that were on the team last year know the heartbreak that it is to lose a national championship game at home,” forward Sachiel Ming said post-game. “You’re heartbroken. You’re on the ground. And today we’re celebrating with the fans.”

On the hunt for their first NCAA Tournament win since 2023, the Orange set the tone early with a persistent man-to-man press, disrupting Sacred Heart’s high possession-style soccer. For Ian McIntyre, head coach of the Orange, this was a key part of the gameplan.

“We understood that they got really talented players,” he said. “They would like the ball and to keep possession… and I think we made it very difficult for them.”

Syracuse’s control of the ball led to multiple scoring chances in the first half. Pedro Gulli’s acrobatic volley in the 31st minute forced a reflex save from Sacred Heart goalkeeper Anthony Suarez. A few minutes later, Dario White’s long-range effort sailed just inches wide of the top right corner. 

At the break, the Orange had outshot Sacred Heart 11 to 4, but were missing a goal to show for it. For junior defender Garrett Holman, who also recalls last fall’s tournament defeat, this is where experience made the difference. 

“Last year against Hofstra, we were on the other end of this,” he said. “So we knew the first goal was going to be the most important.” 

The Orange breakthrough came 15 minutes into the second half. After a low-driven cross from Ming escaped Suarez’s gloves, Syracuse striker Dakota Jonke, who’d followed the ball the entire way, was in a perfect position to just tap it in and put the home team ahead. 

Ming wasn’t done creating danger for McIntyre’s side. Just three minutes later, the winger put in an inch-perfect cross from the left side. Holman, who’d darted into the box moments earlier, towered over the Sacred Heart defense. His header crashed off the post before finding the net. 2-0 Syracuse. 

The goal marked Ming’s team-leading sixth assist of the season, which earned him high praise from his head coach post-game.

“He’s got one of the best left foots in the country,” McIntyre said. 

In the 67th minute of the contest, the visitors followed up with a goal of their own. In a rare counter-attack for The Pioneers, Ivan Morcillo pounced on a loose clearance at the edge of the Syracuse box. His right-footed shot looped over the defense to lodge itself in the top left corner of Juan Martinez-Bastidas’ goal. 

Morcillo’s strike injected confidence into the Sacred Heart attack, which grew into the game as the second half progressed. In the 80th minute of the contest, a video review found Orange center-back Ivan Irinimbabazi guilty of a handball offense in the box. Danny Istanbuli, a captain for The Pioneers, stepped up and converted the spot kick. 

With 10 minutes to go in the contest and both teams level again, Syracuse never lost their composure. 

“A lesser group of young men could have felt sorry for themselves,” McIntyre said. 

In the 84th minute, Irinimbabazi made up for the penalty minutes earlier. Left alone at the backpost on a corner kick, the defender headed home his first goal of the season, for what turned out to be the winner for Syracuse. 

Earlier this month, the Orange pulled off two nail-biting wins in the ACC tournament against Pittsburgh and Stanford. The team’s ability to stay-level headed in close contests has been the difference in post-season play, according to McIntyre. 

“We have talented players, but what we’ve got is character,” he said. “We dig deep.”

The Orange are set to take on the No. 1 seeded Georgetown on Sunday, but they will first take in tonight’s thriller.

“We understand what’s coming down the road, but let’s just enjoy this moment right now,” McIntyre said.
